content.content:
1	# Nxeon marketing site redesign: handoff
2	
3	This package holds everything built during the redesign of the Nxeon marketing site (nxeon.cloud):
4	31 finished pages, the build system that produced them, all assets, and the decisions behind them.
5	
6	The live site is a **Next.js** app. The pages here are **standalone reference implementations**:
7	pixel-accurate, working HTML/CSS/JS that production should reproduce as Next.js components.
8	They are not meant to be dropped in as-is (images are inlined as base64, cross-links point at temporary preview URLs).
9	
10	---
11	
12	## 1. What's in the package
13	
14	| Folder | Contents |
15	|---|---|
16	| `dist/` | The 31 finished pages as single self-contained HTML files, exactly as reviewed and approved. Open any of them in a browser. |
17	| `source/` | The build system: shared CSS/JS/markup, one folder per page, and the Python builders that assemble them. |
18	| `assets/` | Every image the pages use: logos, game artwork, maps, generated backdrops, renders, nav thumbnails. |
19	| `docs/` | This guide, the page inventory, the URL map, and open items. |
20	| `skills/` | Skills for Claude Code: frontend-design (used for this work), nxeon-design-system, nxeon-page-workflow (with verification scripts), nxeon-content-integrity. |
21	| `CLAUDE_CODE_PROMPT.md` | The prompt to continue the work in Claude Code. |
22	
23	### Rebuilding
24	Requirements: Python 3.10+ (standard library only for building). Pillow is only needed to regenerate images; Playwright only for screenshot tools.
25	
26	```
27	cd source
28	python3 build_page.py contact      # rebuild one page into ../dist/nxeon-contact.html
29	sh rebuild_all.sh                  # rebuild everything
30	```
31	The package was verified to rebuild byte-identical output from these folders.
32	
33	---
34	
35	## 2. How the build system works
36	
37	Every page = **shared shell** + **page folder**.
38	
39	**Shared shell** (used by every page):
40	- `source/part1.html`: `<head>` and the global stylesheet (base styles, homepage styles, the nav, the footer).
41	- `source/part2.html`: the SVG icon sprite (`#i-*` symbols), the nav `<header>`, the homepage body, the footer.
42	- `source/part3.html`: global JavaScript (nav behaviour, reveal-on-scroll, counters, homepage modules).
43	- `source/pages/common.css`: styles shared by all inner pages.
44	- `source/pages/aurora.css` + `aurora.js` / `aurora.built.js`: **Aurora UI**, the component design system (see section 3).
45	
46	**Page folder** `source/pages/<slug>/`:
47	- `body.html` (page markup with `{{SPRITE}}`, `{{NAV}}`, `{{FOOTER}}` placeholders)
48	- `page.css`, `page.js`
49	- `meta.json` (title, description, in-page anchors, and the images the page needs as `__IMG_KEY__` placeholders)
50	
51	**`build_page.py <slug>`** stitches shell + folder, inlines images as base64, rewrites nav links so they work
52	from any page, and writes `../dist/nxeon-<slug>.html`.
53	- `assemble.py` builds the homepage (`dist/nxeon.html`).
54	- `build_games2.py` builds the game-servers hub.
55	
56	**Generators** create page folders from data, then call `build_page.py`:
57	
58	| Builder | Produces | Data lives in |
59	|---|---|---|
60	| `build_gs2.py game` / `build_gs2.py loc` | Minecraft hosting page, Minecraft in Singapore (the conversion template for all game servers) | `MC` + `TIERS` in `build_gameserver.py`, `SPEC`/`TINFO` in `build_gs2.py`, `LOC` in `build_location.py` |
61	| `loc_render.py <slug>` | VPS location pages (Singapore, Germany) with real dot maps | `build_location.py` (`LOC`), `assets/maps/` |
62	| `build_usecase.py <slug>` | WordPress / Docker use-case pages | `USE` in `build_usecase.py`, `EXTRA` in `use_extra.py` |
63	| `build_compare.py <slug>` | Nxeon vs competitor pages (template in `pages/_cmp/`) | `CMP` in `build_compare.py` |
64	| `build_modsgame.py minecraft` | NxLabs mods-per-game page | `GAMES` in `build_modsgame.py`, `pages/mc_catalog.json` |
65	| `build_modsbrowse.py` | "All Minecraft mods" paginated browse page | `pages/mc_catalog.json` |
66	| `build_modpage.py` | Individual mod page (Lithium) | `LITHIUM` dict in `build_modpage.py`, `mod_tags.py` |
67	| `build_blogpost.py` | Blog article template (Vaultwarden) | `A` dict in `build_blogpost.py` |
68	| `build_bloghub.py` | Blog hub | `P` list in `build_bloghub.py` |
69	| `build_blogvisuals.py` | Blog cover visual system (archetypes + logos + palettes) | `GUIDES` in `build_blogvisuals.py`, `pages/_logos.json` |
70	
71	Shared components used by several builders: `mods_ui.py` (mod cards), `mod_tags.py` (tag-driven illustrations),
72	`pages/_shield.*` (Nxeon Shield DDoS section, extracted from the homepage), `pages/_modscards.css` (cards + carousels),
73	`pages/_gs*.{css,js}` (game-server builder, world picker, sticky deploy bar).
74	
75	Class-name rule used throughout: every page's classes are namespaced to avoid collisions with the global stylesheet.
76	Several bugs during the build came from collisions (`.mcard`, `.shr`, `.sp`, `.bar`, the `wait` helper).
77	Check new names against `part1.html`, `common.css` and `aurora.css` before using them.
78	
79	---
80	
81	## 3. Design system
82	
83	**Typography:** Plus Jakarta Sans (display + body), a monospace for code and data. Fonts are in `source/fonts/`.
84	
85	**Colour:** dark base (`--bg` near #060913), ink #EEF1FA, secondary ink ~#A9B1CE, muted ~#7A83A6.
86	Aurora accents: cyan #3EDCF2, blue #4E6BFF, violet #7B5CFF/#9B6BFF, magenta #E04BD6/#FF5FD7, mint #3FD89A, amber #FFB36B/#FFD27A (reserved for "custom / enterprise").
87	
88	**Aurora UI components** (`pages/aurora.css`, `aurora.js`; live reference page: `dist/nxeon-aurora-ui.html`):
89	buttons (`au-btn`, `--glass`, `--ghost`), segmented control (`au-seg`), cards with pointer spotlight (`au-card`),
90	search (`au-search`), range slider (`au-range`), toggle (`au-toggle`), chips, animated icon set (`data-au-icon`),
91	count-up (`data-au-count`, formats with thousands separators), gauges, sparklines, toasts (`auToast`),
92	FAQ accordion (`.faq details`, smooth height, soft glow that fades out past each item).
93	
94	**Glass card tiers** (homepage and inner pages): *quiet* (neutral glass, colour only as a top hairline, lights up on hover),
95	*medium* (soft tint of the card's product colour), *vivid* (full glow, used sparingly: the featured VPS price card, the Creator panel).
96	Palettes follow meaning: mint = savings/success, amber = effort or custom/enterprise, brand colours for competitors.
97	
98	**Nav** (`part2.html` header + `part1.html` NAV v2 styles + `part3.html` Navigation script):
99	- Top level: Products (mega menu), Matrix, Pricing, Compare, NxLabs (inline "Game Mod Store" badge), Company (menu); right: Status pill, Log in, Get started.
100	- **Products** uses Nxeon's real columns: Compute / Storage and network / Web essentials / By use case (on its own soft panel, with "All features"), plus a popular game servers strip with artwork.
101	- **Company:** About, Blog, Security, Contact, Affiliate program, Status, plus the latest guide.
102	- One shared dropdown morphs between menus.
103	  - **Mouse:** hover opens with intent delay.
104	  - **Keyboard:** click or ArrowDown opens; Escape closes and returns focus.
105	  - **Closed state:** the dropdown can't be tabbed into.
106	- Full-screen sheet on mobile.
107	- Logged-in state should drop "My account" / "Back to portal" into the Log in / Get started slot.
108	
109	**Matrix page** deliberately uses its own language (after Cursor / Grok / OpenClaw):
110	- **Opening:** black canvas, a horizon glow and a big prompt box.
111	- **Product:** a realistic app window on painted backdrops, with a tech-logo row.
112	- **Buttons:** white.
113	- **Motion:** only where it is the product.
114	
115	**Blog cover visual system:** each guide gets an automatic cover.
116	- **Archetypes by topic:** flow, terminal, shield, stack, vault, chart, route. Game guides use game artwork.
117	- **Logos:** official brand logos from its tags, via Simple Icons (`pages/_logos.json`).
118	- **Palettes:** chosen by category.
119	- **Motion:** covers show their finished state and only play ambient motion on hover.
120	
121	---
122	
123	## 4. Design direction (what the stakeholder asked for; keep to it)
124	
125	- **Premium and considered, never "vibe coded".** Too many animations read as cheap; too plain reads as a regression.
126	  Target: motion only where it demonstrates the product, confident typography, generous space, real product UI.
127	- **Real data only.** Every claim, price, count and list came from the live nxeon.cloud pages or the source it cites.
128	  Where data didn't exist, it is marked as a placeholder (see OPEN-ITEMS.md). Never invent customer quotes, stats or specs.
129	- **Conversion pages must not be brushed off.** Game-server pages carry:
130	  - a deploy console in the hero
131	  - the Nxeon Shield DDoS section
132	  - a "Choose your world" picker with CPU, RAM and NVMe resources plus a fit calculator
133	  - a sticky deploy bar
134	  - custom-server CTAs (gold) linking to `/contact?topic=custom`
135	  - an objection-handling FAQ
136	- **Glassmorphism with restraint:** dark crisp glass, colour in controlled places, no grain, no milky washes.
137	- **Game hero images:** game page = the game's own art; game × location page = game art blended into the city image.
138	
139	---
140	
141	## 5. Page inventory
142	
143	| Page | File (dist/) | Production route | Built by | Source of content |
144	|---|---|---|---|---|
145	| Homepage | nxeon.html | / | assemble.py | live homepage |
146	| Matrix (flagship) | nxeon-matrix.html | /matrix | pages/matrix | live /matrix |

2	
3	Copy everything below the line into Claude Code, from the root of the Nxeon marketing site repository,

5	
6	---
7	
8	You're continuing a redesign of the Nxeon marketing website (nxeon.cloud), a Next.js app. A complete design package is in `./design-handoff/`:
9	- `dist/`: 31 finished, approved pages as standalone HTML. These are the source of truth for how each page should look and behave.
10	- `source/`: the build system that produced them (shared CSS/JS, one folder per page, Python generators with the page data).
11	- `assets/`: every image, logo and backdrop.
12	- `docs/HANDOFF.md`: architecture, design system, design direction and page inventory.
13	- `docs/OPEN-ITEMS.md`: unconfirmed data, pages still to build, and issues found on the live site.
14	- `docs/url-map.json`: maps the temporary preview links inside the pages to production routes.
15	
16	First, install the project skills: `mkdir -p .claude/skills && cp -r design-handoff/skills/frontend-design design-handoff/skills/nxeon-* .claude/skills/`, then `pip install playwright pillow && playwright install chromium` for the verification scripts. Use `nxeon-design-system`, `nxeon-page-workflow` and `nxeon-content-integrity` on every page, and `frontend-design` for any new design.
17	
18	**Read `docs/HANDOFF.md` and `docs/OPEN-ITEMS.md` fully before writing any code.** Then explore this repository: its routing, layout, styling approach, existing components, how pages get content, and anything tied to auth, the dashboard, checkout or the deploy flow. Summarise what you find and propose a porting plan before starting. Wait for my go-ahead on the plan.
19	
20	## Goal
21	Bring the redesign into this codebase as real Next.js pages and components that match the `dist/` pages visually and behaviourally, on desktop (1440px) and mobile (390px), while keeping everything the live site does today working: auth links, dashboard, checkout, deploy links, SEO metadata and existing routes.
22	
23	## Porting order
24	1. **Foundation:**
25	   - design tokens and global styles
26	   - Plus Jakarta Sans
27	   - the Aurora UI component library (`source/pages/aurora.css`, `aurora.js`; reference page `dist/nxeon-aurora-ui.html`)
28	   - the new Nav (desktop mega menus and mobile sheet)
29	   - the Footer
30	   - the shared Nxeon Shield section
31	2. **Homepage** (`dist/nxeon.html`).
32	3. **Matrix** (`dist/nxeon-matrix.html`), the flagship. It uses its own visual language; see HANDOFF section 3.
33	4. **Game-server conversion template:**
34	   - Minecraft hosting and Minecraft in Singapore
35	   - built as one data-driven template, so every game and every game × region page comes from data
36	5. **Pricing**, then Compare and Nxeon vs DigitalOcean (a data-driven comparison template).
37	6. **NxLabs:**
38	   - the hub, then the mods-per-game page and the browse page
39	   - the individual mod page, which has three layers (automatic from source data, tag-driven illustrations, curated highlights)
40	7. **Blog:**
41	   - the hub, then the article template
42	   - the cover visual system: archetypes plus Simple Icons logos from tags plus category palettes, with game art for game guides
43	8. **Contact:** routed topics, adaptive fields and `?topic=` deep links. Wire it to the real endpoint.
44	9. **Product and supporting pages:** VPS, Web hosting, Business email, Domains, NxCloud, Migrate, Free VPS, Free Minecraft, the Singapore and Germany VPS pages, WordPress, Docker and Valheim.
45	
46	## Rules
47	- **Match the approved designs.** For each page, run `.claude/skills/nxeon-page-workflow/scripts/verify_page.py` and `compare_screens.py` against the matching `dist/` file, at 1440px and 390px, and look at the images. Fix differences before moving on. Don't "improve" the design unasked.
48	- **Design direction:**
49	  - Premium and considered, never busy.
50	  - Motion only where it demonstrates the product, and always respect `prefers-reduced-motion`.
51	  - Dark crisp glass with colour in controlled places, no grain.
52	  - Keep the keyboard behaviour of menus, carousels and FAQs.
53	- **Real data only:**
54	  - Keep copy, prices and counts exactly as in `dist/` unless OPEN-ITEMS says otherwise.
55	  - Catalogue-driven content (mods, blog posts, games, plans) must come from the data the live site already uses, not the snapshots baked into `dist/`.
56	  - Never invent claims, specs, reviews or statistics. If something is unknown, leave a clearly marked TODO and tell me.
57	- **Items to confirm with me before shipping:** everything in OPEN-ITEMS section A, including the game-server prices and CPU/NVMe specs, which are currently placeholders.
58	- **Fix the live-site issues** in OPEN-ITEMS section C as you port each affected page, and tell me each time.
59	- **Assets:** move images into `/public` (use `next/image`) rather than inlining base64, and replace every preview link using `docs/url-map.json`.
60	- **Accessibility:** semantic landmarks, visible focus states, labelled controls, alt text, and contrast at least as good as the originals.
61	- **Performance:** lazy-load below-the-fold imagery and ship no unused JS.
62	- **Work in small, reviewable steps:** one page or component per commit, with a short summary of what changed and anything I need to decide.
63	
64	## After the port
65	Continue with the pages listed in OPEN-ITEMS section B, reusing the established templates and design system. For any page that exists on the live site, read its live content first and build from that. Ask me for anything you can't source, such as competitor logos or missing routes.

1	---
2	name: nxeon-design-system
3	description: The Nxeon marketing site's design system and design direction. Use it whenever you build, port, restyle or review any Nxeon page, section or component (nav, footer, heroes, cards, pricing, game-server pages, NxLabs mod pages, blog, Matrix, contact), or when choosing colours, type, glass effects, animation or layout for nxeon.cloud, even if the user doesn't say "design system".
4	---
5	
6	# Nxeon design system
7	
8	The approved reference pages are in `design-handoff/dist/`. The design system source is in `design-handoff/source/pages/aurora.css` and `aurora.js`, with the live component gallery in `dist/nxeon-aurora-ui.html`. Treat the dist pages as the source of truth. When unsure how something should look, open the matching dist page and match it.
9	
10	## Direction (set by the stakeholder over many review rounds; follow it)
11	
12	- **Premium and considered, never "vibe coded".** Scattered animation, glows on everything and toy mock-ups read as cheap. Over-correcting into flat, empty pages was also rejected as "too far back". Aim between the two: confident type, generous space, real product UI, and one memorable moment per page.
13	- **Motion only where it demonstrates the product** (a console building, a plan being approved, a picker resizing a world), or where it answers a user action. Nothing loops for decoration. Always honour `prefers-reduced-motion`.
14	- **Glass with restraint:** dark crisp glass, colour in controlled places, no grain, no milky full-page washes.
15	- **Conversion pages carry strong CTAs:** game-server and pricing pages must not be "brushed off" (see the game-server pattern below).
16	- **Real content only;** see the `nxeon-content-integrity` skill.
17	
18	## Foundations
19	
20	- **Type:** Plus Jakarta Sans for display and body, plus a monospace for code, logs and data. Display headlines at weight 700 to 800 with tight tracking (about -0.04em). Keep body line length under about 70 characters.
21	- **Base colours:** background near #060913, ink #EEF1FA, secondary ink about #A9B1CE, muted about #7A83A6, hairlines rgba(255,255,255,.08).
22	- **Aurora accents:** cyan #3EDCF2, blue #4E6BFF, violet #7B5CFF/#9B6BFF, magenta #E04BD6/#FF5FD7, mint #3FD89A.
23	- **Colour carries meaning:**
24	  - mint = savings, success, live
25	  - amber (#FFB36B/#FFD27A) = custom or enterprise, or "effort"
26	  - each product and brand keeps its own colour (VPS blue, Game Servers magenta, Web cyan, Email violet, Domains teal)
27	- **Section labels:** a small uppercase label is used sparingly, never on every heading.
28	
29	## Components (Aurora UI)
30	
31	`au-btn` (plus `--glass` and `--ghost`), `au-seg` (segmented control with a sliding pill), `au-card` (pointer spotlight), `au-search`, `au-range`, `au-toggle`, chips, the animated icon set (`data-au-icon`, `data-grad`), `data-au-count` (count-up with thousands separators), gauges, sparklines, `auToast`, and the FAQ accordion (`.faq details`).
32	
33	- **FAQ open state:** a soft glow layer (`details::before`) fades out beyond the item. Never paint a background inside the box, because it produced hard, clipped edges.
34	- **Glass card tiers** (homepage pattern):
35	  - *Quiet* (most cards): neutral glass, product colour only as a top hairline, lights up on hover.
36	  - *Medium:* a soft tint of the product colour.
37	  - *Vivid:* reserved for one or two focal cards per page.
38	
39	## Signature patterns (see references/patterns.md for details)
40	
41	- **Nav:**
42	  - Products mega menu with Nxeon's real columns (Compute / Storage and network / Web essentials / By use case, with "All features") plus a popular game servers strip. Direct links to Matrix, Pricing and Compare. NxLabs with an inline "Game Mod Store" badge. A Company menu.
43	  - One shared dropdown morphs between menus: hover intent, ArrowDown to enter, Escape returns focus, closed menus aren't tabbable.
44	  - A full-screen sheet on mobile.
45	- **Game-server conversion page:** a deploy console hero (name, version, loader cards, players with avatars, NxLabs mods, region cards, live CPU/RAM/NVMe plus price) that runs a short in-card deploy. Then:
46	  - the Nxeon Shield DDoS section
47	  - "Choose your world": a voxel island, resources and a "Will it fit?" meter
48	  - a custom-server option (gold)
49	  - a sticky deploy bar
50	  - an objection-handling FAQ
51	
52	  Game page hero = the game's own art. Game × location hero = game art blended into the city.
53	- **Matrix (flagship):** its own language, after Cursor, Grok and OpenClaw.
54	  - **Opening:** a black canvas with a horizon glow and one big prompt box.
55	  - **Product:** a realistic app window on painted backdrops, with a tech-logo row.
56	  - **Style:** white buttons, neutral greys, motion only in the product.
57	- **Blog covers:** archetype by topic (flow, terminal, shield, stack, vault, chart, route), brand logos from tags (Simple Icons), and a palette by category. Game guides use game art. Covers rest in their finished state and animate only on hover.
58	- **NxLabs mod page:** three layers. Automatic from source data (summary, sides, loaders, license, gallery), tag-driven illustrations, and curated highlights only for featured mods.
59	
60	## Pitfalls that caused real bugs (check every time)
61	
62	- **Class-name collisions** with the global stylesheet (`.mcard`, `.shr`, `.sp`, `.bar`, `.lh`, `.pk`) broke layouts. Namespace page classes and grep the globals before naming.
63	- **Global JS names:** a page redefined `wait`, which is already a global helper, and the whole script died. Prefix page helpers.
64	- **SVG `<use href="#i-…">` icons break if a link rewriter touches them.** They also need a viewBox/size and `fill:none; stroke:currentColor`.
65	- **CSS `height` on an SVG `rect` with a shared class** overrides the attribute. That happened to `.bar`.
66	- **Chips and segmented controls set programmatically** must dispatch the same event the component listens to (range fill, `au-seg` pill).
67	- **Always screenshot at 1440 and 390 and look before calling anything done.** Most regressions were only visible in screenshots.
68

1	---
2	name: nxeon-page-workflow
3	description: The end-to-end workflow for building, porting or redesigning any page of the Nxeon marketing site (nxeon.cloud), from sourcing live content to verified, screenshot-checked output. Use it whenever you create a new Nxeon page, port a design-handoff page into the Next.js app, rebuild a template (game servers, locations, comparisons, mods, blog), or fix a page, even for small changes.
4	---
5	
6	# Building or porting an Nxeon page
7	
8	Follow these steps in order. Skipping the verification step is how most regressions in this project happened.
9	
10	## 1. Source the real content first
11	- If the page exists on nxeon.cloud, read the live page before designing. Extract the real claims, prices, counts, lists, FAQ answers and links.
12	- If a catalogue is involved (mods, blog posts, games, plans), use the same data source the live site uses.
13	- If data doesn't exist, don't invent it. Use a clearly labelled placeholder and list it for the user (see `nxeon-content-integrity`).
14	- Note any live-site bugs you notice (typos, contradictions, broken counters) and report them.
15	
16	## 2. Pick the pattern
17	- Check `design-handoff/docs/HANDOFF.md` (page inventory) and the `nxeon-design-system` skill's patterns table. Reuse an existing template before inventing a new layout.
18	- For a new page, propose the concept to the user in a few sentences before building: what the hero is, which sections, where motion goes and why.
19	
20	## 3. Build
21	- Match the approved dist page if one exists. Don't "improve" it unasked.
22	- Namespace page-level class names, and check them against the global styles before use.
23	- Keep motion to what demonstrates the product, and support `prefers-reduced-motion`.
24	- Keep keyboard behaviour: menus, carousels, tabs, FAQ, forms.
25	- Replace preview links (claude.ai/artifact/…) with production routes from `docs/url-map.json`.
26	
27	## 4. Verify (every time)
28	Run the checks in `scripts/`:
29	- `python scripts/verify_page.py <url-or-file>`: loads the page at 1440 and 390, and reports:
30	  - JavaScript errors
31	  - horizontal overflow on mobile
32	  - images that failed to load
33	  - icon references that were rewritten or broken
34	  - whether the nav opens
35	
36	  It saves screenshots. Fix every reported problem.
37	- `python scripts/compare_screens.py <reference.html> <candidate-url> --out compare.png`: side-by-side screenshots of the approved design and your version at both widths. Look at the image. Differences in spacing, colour, type or missing elements must be fixed or explained.
38	- Test interactions by hand-scripting them (open menus, submit forms, change pickers) and assert on the resulting state, not just the absence of errors.
39	- Re-check anything a previous fix touched. Fixes in shared styles (nav, FAQ, cards) affect every page.
40	
41	## 5. Report
42	Tell the user, briefly:
43	- what was built and where
44	- what was verified
45	- anything that needs their decision: placeholders, unknown routes, data to confirm
46	- live-site issues found
47	
48	Lead with what they need to act on.
49	
50	## Lessons from this project
51	- **Screenshots find what error checks miss:** clipped glows, invisible icons, orphan grid rows, headlines wrapping to four lines, and content hidden behind other content.
52	- **Bulk edits across built files are dangerous.** A string marker that also appeared in the stylesheet caused a patch to wipe out page content. Rebuild from source instead of patching outputs, and verify each page's own content is still there afterwards.
53	- **Game art first seen in the grid can repeat side by side.** Interleave, and vary the crop.
54	- **Keep grids full:** avoid a lone card on the last row.
55

1	---
2	name: nxeon-content-integrity
3	description: Rules for every piece of content on the Nxeon marketing site: which facts are verified, which are placeholders awaiting confirmation, how to source new data, how to write in Nxeon's voice, and what claims to avoid. Use it whenever you write or change copy, prices, specs, counts, reviews, comparisons, mod or game data, blog content, or logos on nxeon.cloud pages, including when porting existing pages.
4	---
5	
6	# Content integrity for nxeon.cloud
7	
8	The stakeholder rejected work built on assumed content. Pages only came together when they were built from the real product. Hold this line on every page.
9	
10	## The rule
11	Every claim, price, count, spec, list, quote and FAQ answer must come from one of:
12	1. The live nxeon.cloud page (or its data source) for that topic.
13	2. The primary source the page cites (for example Modrinth, GitHub or CurseForge for a mod; a competitor's own pricing page for a comparison, noting the date checked).
14	3. The stakeholder, directly.
15	
16	If none of these has it, **don't invent it.** Use a clearly marked placeholder (`TODO(confirm): …` in code, or a visible "preview" note where appropriate) and list it in your report.
17	
18	## Currently unconfirmed (don't present these as final)
19	- **Game-server tier prices** (Minecraft 1 GB $2.99 … 16 GB $32.99): the pricing panel marks them as preview figures. Only Valheim's are marked live.
20	- **Game-server vCPU and NVMe per tier:** placeholders modelled on the VPS plans (`SPEC` in build_gs2.py).
21	- **Fit-calculator and modpack-guide figures:** sizing heuristics, not measured data.
22	- **Review badges** (Trustpilot 4.9/312, HostAdvice 4.8/148, Google 4.9/205): copied from the live site, where they link to `#`. Verify them and link them to the real profiles.
23	- **Routes:** Dedicated IPv4, AI apps and agents, NxCloud, game × location pages, and the mods browse page.
24	- See `design-handoff/docs/OPEN-ITEMS.md` for the full list.
25	
26	## Verified facts in use (examples)
27	- **VPS plans:** 2/4/8/16 GB, 1/2/3/4 vCPU, 25/50/80/120 GB NVMe. Regular $12.78/$18.70/$30.22/$47.50 per month, or $10.22/$14.96/$24.18/$38.00 on annual terms.
28	- **Regions:** Singapore and Falkenstein (Germany).
29	- **NxLabs:** 64,709 mods, 33 games, 14B downloads, verified against Modrinth, SpigotMC, Thunderstore, GitHub, Nexus Mods and uMod. Free, no account needed. "Add to my server" for Nxeon customers.
30	- **Matrix:** up to 6 parallel consoles; mirror mode across 2 to 6 servers; per-console choice of Anthropic API key or the Claude CLI with Claude Pro or Max; plan approval before anything runs.
31	- **Contact:** support@nxeon.cloud, dashboard tickets, reply within one business day.
32	- **Numbers are snapshots.** Catalogue counts change, so production should read them from the live data.
33	
34	## Known contradictions on the live site (resolve, don't copy)
35	- Support: "within one business day" vs "24/7" / "around the clock". Ask which is true.
36	- Pricing: "never increases at renewal" vs "intro price, then regular price".
37	- Managed vs self-managed positioning.
38	- Regions: the homepage's global network lists 7 cities, but only Singapore and Germany exist.
39	- Naming: "Claude CLI" vs "Claude Code". The product is Claude Code; keep the site consistent.
40	- Blog: the unrelated game-server screenshot in non-game articles, and the public `#seobatch` tag.
41	
42	## Voice
43	Straight-talking and specific, like the blog's "no fluff, just what actually works".
44	- **Plain words:** plain verbs, sentence case, and name things the way users think of them.
45	- **Buttons:** say exactly what happens ("Deploy 4 GB · $8.99/mo", "Talk to us about a custom server").
46	- **Honesty:** comparisons state where the competitor wins. When a claim is a heuristic, say so ("varies with the pack you run").
47	
48	## Claims and marks to avoid
49	- **No invented testimonials, customer counts, benchmarks or performance percentages.** The live site's "illustrative use-cases" are labelled as not testimonials; keep that honesty.
50	- **No implied partnership with Anthropic** or any vendor.
51	- **Brand logos** (from Simple Icons or the vendor) identify technologies only. Keep the site's existing trademark disclaimer wherever logos appear in quantity.
52	- **Game artwork** identifies the game. Don't use it to suggest endorsement, and don't reproduce characters in generated imagery.
53

1	---
2	name: frontend-design
3	description: Guidance for distinctive, intentional visual design when building new UI or reshaping an existing one. Helps with aesthetic direction, typography, and making choices that don't read as templated defaults.
4	license: Complete terms in LICENSE.txt
5	---
6	
7	# Frontend Design
8	
9	Approach this as the design lead at a design studio known for giving every client a distinct visual identity that is not mistaken for anyone else's. This client has already rejected proposals that felt cliché or templated, and is paying for a distinctive point of view: make deliberate, opinionated choices about palette, typography, and layout that are specific to this brief, and take aesthetic risk if justified.
10	
11	## Ground your designs in the subject matter
12	
13	If the brief does not identify what the product or subject matter is, identify it yourself before designing, and confirm with the client. You can come up with one concrete subject, the design's audience, and the design's primary job, as a proposal. If there's any information in your memory about the client's preferences or context about what they're building, use that as a hint. The subject's industry, subject matter, materials, and vernacular are where distinctive visual choices come from — a design for a toy for girls aged 8–11 will be very aesthetically different from a dashboard for financial analysts. Build with the brief's real content and subject matter throughout.
14	
15	## Design principles
16	
17	For web designs, the hero is the first thing viewers will see. Open with the most characteristic thing in the subject's world, in the form that is most appropriate: a headline, an image, an animation, a live demo, an interactive moment, or other treatments. Be deliberate with your choice: a big number with a small label, supporting stats, and a gradient accent is the default treatment, so only use it if that's truly the best option.
18	
19	Typography carries the personality of the page. You don't need a different typeface for display or headline text and body content: use one family or two, and if two, make them clearly distinct.
20	
21	Choose your typefaces deliberately, not the default families you would reach for on any other project, and set a clear type scale following the default guidance of The Elements of Typographic Style with intentional weights, widths, and spacing. When type is used as a headline or visual element, use the type treatment itself as an active part of the design, not a neutral delivery vehicle for the content.
22	
23	Default to line lengths of less than 80 characters. Serif typefaces can have slightly longer line lengths; give serif body text slightly more line-height than a sans-serif.
24	
25	Avoid these default typographic treatments; they are the commonest tells of a generated page:
26	- Accenting just a single word or phrase in a headline, like putting one word in italic/bold or a different color.
27	- Using all caps for labels.
28	- Adding unnecessary typographic labels above content.
29	
30	Visual structure is information. Structural devices like outlines, borders, numbering, eyebrows, dividers, labels, etc., encode useful information about the content rather than decorate it. Many generic designs use numbered markers (01 / 02 / 03), but that's only appropriate if the content actually is a sequence — like a stepped process or a timeline. Before adding numbered markers, check the content really is a sequence.
31	
32	Use non-user-triggered motion sparingly and deliberately, only to draw attention. A single orchestrated moment — one page-load sequence or one reveal — lands better than scattered effects; fade-and-slide-up entrances on each section and hover transitions on every card are the generic default and read as AI-generated. Motion that answers a person's action (opening, expanding, confirming) is welcome when it shows what changed.
33	
34	Consider written content carefully. Often a design brief may not contain real content, and it's up to you to come up with copy and placeholder content. Copy can make a design feel as templated as the design itself. See the below section on writing for more guidance.
35	
36	## Process: plan, review against the brief, build, critique
37	
38	For calibration, AI-generated design right now clusters around some traits:
39	1. a warm cream background (near #F4F1EA) with a high-contrast serif display and a terracotta or warm-clay accent (often near #D97757 — Anthropic's own Claude-interaction accent, so on a user's brief it reads as a tell);
40	2. a near-black background with a single bright acid-green or vermilion accent;
41	3. a broadsheet-style layout with hairline rules, zero border-radius, and dense newspaper-like columns;
42	4. the SaaS-card kit: content chopped into identical rounded cards, one border-radius on everything regardless of hierarchy, the same soft grey shadow (rgba(0,0,0,.1)) under each, and gradient washes as decoration;
43	5. template chrome that appears whatever the subject: a tracked-out ALL-CAPS eyebrow label above every heading; meta strings joined with middle dots ('A · B · C'); labels built as 'WORD — fragment' with a spaced em dash; tinted near-black (#0B0B0B, #111) standing in for black; a monospace face for small data labels; a '→' appended to link and button text.
44	
45	All traits are legitimate for some briefs, but they are defaults rather than choices, and they appear regardless of subject. Where the brief pins down a visual direction, follow it exactly — the brief's own words always win, including when it asks for one of these looks. Where it leaves an axis free, don't spend that freedom on one of these defaults. As with a hired human designer, there's often a careful balance between doing what you're good at and taking each project as a chance to experiment and learn.
46	
47	Work in two passes. First, brainstorm a short design plan based on the client's design brief: create a compact token system with color, type, layout, and principles.
48	- Color: describe the core base palette as 4–6 named hex values.
49	- Type: the typefaces and their roles.
50	- Layout: a layout concept, using one-sentence prose descriptions and ASCII wireframes to ideate and compare. Include alignment guidance; should the content be left aligned, center aligned, justified?
51	- Principles: the high-level guidance for what makes this page unique.
52	
53	Then review that plan against the brief before building: if any part of it reads like the generic default you would produce for any similar page (work through a similar prompt to see if you arrive somewhere similar) rather than a choice made for this specific brief — revise that part, say what you changed and why. Only after you've confirmed the relative uniqueness of your design plan should you start to write the code, following the revised plan.
54	
55	When writing the code, be careful of structuring your CSS selector specificities. It's easy to generate CSS classes that cancel each other out (especially with a type-based selector like .section and an element-based selector like .cta). This can happen often with padding/margin between sections.
56	
57	## Restraint and self-critique
58	
59	Spend your boldness in one place. Let one element be the memorable thing, keep everything around it quiet and disciplined, and cut any decoration that does not serve the brief. Build to a quality floor without announcing it: responsive down to mobile, visible keyboard focus, reduced motion respected, visually accessible, harmonious color palettes. Critique your own work as you build, taking screenshots to review if your environment supports it — a picture is worth 1000 tokens. Consider Chanel's advice: before leaving the house, take a look in the mirror and remove one accessory. Human creatives have memory and always try to do something new, so if you have a space to quickly jot down notes about what you've tried, it can help you in future passes.
60	
61	## More on writing in design
62	
63	Words appear in a design for one reason: to make it easier to understand and use. They are design content, not decoration. Bring the same intentionality and minimalism to copywriting that you would bring to spacing and color. Before writing anything, ask what the design needs to say, and how it can best be said to help the person navigate the experience.
64	
65	Write from the end user's perspective. Name things by what users will understand in simple language, not by how the system is built. A user manages notifications, not webhook config. Describe what something is or does in plain terms rather than selling it. Being specific and legible to new users is always better than being clever.
66	
67	Use active voice as default. A CTA says exactly what happens when it is used: "Save changes," not "Submit." An action keeps the same name through the whole flow, so the button that says "Publish" produces a toast that says "Published." The vocabulary of an interface is the signposting for someone navigating the product. Cohesion and consistency are how people learn their way around.
68	
69	Treat failure and emptiness as moments for direction, not mood. Explain what went wrong and how to fix it, in the interface's voice rather than a person's. Errors don't apologize, and they are never vague about what happened. An empty screen is an invitation to act.
70	
71	Keep the tone conversational: plain verbs, sentence case, no filler, with tone matched to the brand and the audience. Let each written element do exactly one job.
72

FAQ

Questions about Matrix

What is Nxeon Matrix?

Matrix is Nxeon’s flagship AI app builder. It gives you a multi-console workspace where you can open up to six live build consoles at once, each one an AI agent building a different project, or the same prompt mirrored across several servers. Everything runs on the Nxeon VPS you already have, so there’s no local setup.

Can I really build several apps at the same time?

Yes. Matrix runs 1 to 6 consoles in parallel, each independent, each building on a server you choose. You can also use mirror mode to send one prompt to 2 to 6 consoles at once and compare the variations they produce.

Do I need an Anthropic API key, or can I use my Claude subscription?

Either, and you choose per console. Paste your own Anthropic API key for metered, pay-as-you-go builds, or use the Claude CLI that comes pre-installed on your Nxeon VPS and sign in with your Claude Pro or Max subscription for flat-rate building.

What can I build with it?

Anything you can run on a server: a SaaS product, a REST or webhook API, a Discord bot, a landing page or full site, internal tools and automations. You describe it, approve the plan, and Matrix configures your server and builds it.

Where do the apps run?

On your own Nxeon VPS. Matrix builds and runs each project on infrastructure you already have with us, so you own the code and the machine. No lock-in, and you can build from anywhere in the browser.

### Tokens (from `source/part1.html` `:root`, confirmed against `aurora.css`)

**Color:**
- Backgrounds: `--bg:#060913`, `--bg-2:#080D1C`, `--surface:#0C1328`, `--surface-2:#111A34`, `--surface-3:#16213F`
- Hairlines: `--line:rgba(138,160,255,.12)`, `--line-2:rgba(138,160,255,.2)`, `--line-3:rgba(160,180,255,.34)`
- Ink: `--ink:#E9EDFA`, `--ink-2:#B6BEDA`, `--muted:#8792B4`
- Brand/product: `--blue:#1463FF`, `--blue-hi:#3B7DFF`, `--link:#86A8FF`, `--indigo:#4B2EF2`
- Aurora accents: `--cyan:#3EDCF2`, `--purple:#7B3AF5`, `--magenta:#E04BD6`, `--green:#3FD89A`, `--amber:#F2B64B`
  (design-system skill docs also cite `#4E6BFF` blue, `#9B6BFF` violet, `#FF5FD7` magenta, `#FFD27A` amber as secondary shade variants used across pages — both are correct, these are 2-stop gradients per accent)
- Gradient: `--aurora: linear-gradient(90deg,#3EDCF2 0%,#0A66FF 36%,#4B2EF2 68%,#8B3DF5 100%)`
- `color-scheme: dark` is forced everywhere — **there is no light theme**; `:root[data-theme="light"]` is referenced defensively in a media query but no light-theme rule set exists in the files I found.

**Radii:** `--r-xl:24px; --r-lg:18px; --r-md:12px; --r-sm:8px` (plus Aurora's own `--au-r3` used on cards/buttons, defined in `aurora.css`).

**Type:** `--f-display` / `--f-body`: "Plus Jakarta Sans", system-ui fallback stack. `--f-mono`: "JetBrains Mono", ui-monospace fallback. Display weight 700–800, tight tracking ~ -0.04em per the skill doc (I did not measure this in CSS directly but it matches what's in `part1.html` heading rules).

**Layout:** `--container:1240px`, `--nav-h:68px`. Base font-size 17px, line-height 1.6.

### Aurora UI component library (`source/pages/aurora.css`, `aurora.js`; live reference `dist/nxeon-aurora-ui.html`)

Read directly from `aurora.css` selectors (249 lines) and cross-checked against the design-system
skill's own list. Every component below has a working CSS implementation in this file:

| Component | Selector(s) | One-line description |
|---|---|---|
| Glass surface | `.au-glass` | Base translucent panel: gradient glass background, hairline border, soft top highlight. |
| Spotlight card | `.au-card` | Glass card with a pointer-tracked radial "spotlight" ring that fades in on hover and lifts the card. |
| Button | `.au-btn` (+ `--glass`, `--ghost`) | Gradient pill button with an animated sheen sweep on hover; `--glass` variant adds a spinning conic-gradient border on hover; `--ghost` is bordered/transparent. Has `.is-loading` (spinner) and `.is-done` (green) states. |
| Ripple | `.au-ripple` | Radial ripple burst on click, layered under button content. |

| Range slider | `.au-range` + `.au-bub` | Custom-styled `<input type=range>` with a gradient fill track and a floating value bubble that appears on hover/focus/drag. |
| Text field | `.au-field` | Floating-label input/textarea with focus glow, inline hint text, a green "valid" check dot, and a shake animation on error. |
| Search box | `.au-search` | Pill search input with a `kbd` hint, clear button, and a blurred glow ring that grows in on focus. |
| Segmented control | `.au-seg` | Pill-group of buttons with a sliding "pill" background that animates between selections. |
| Accordion / FAQ | `.au-acc details`, `.faq details` | Custom `<details>` accordion; the FAQ variant has a soft glow layer (`::before`) that fades out past the item edge rather than a hard background fill. |
| Chip / badge | `.au-chip` | Pill label with a pulsing status dot (`.d`); `.warn` variant recolors the dot amber. |
| Toast | `.au-toasts` / `.au-toast` | Bottom-right stacked toast notifications with an auto-dismiss progress bar; `auToast()` JS helper referenced in HANDOFF. |
| Progress bar | `.au-prog` | Bar with a shimmering highlight sweep animation. |
| Skeleton loader | `.au-skel` | Shimmering placeholder block for loading states. |
| Gauge | `.au-gauge` | Circular SVG gauge with lit tick marks and an animated count-up value in the center. |
| Sparkline | `.au-spark` | Small inline line chart with a hover point + tooltip. |
| Bar chart | `.au-bars` | Vertical animated bar chart, bars grow in on view, hoverable with value callouts. |
| Wave | `.au-wave` | Decorative animated SVG line/wave path. |
| Animated icon set | `.au-ic`, `data-au-icon`, `.au-tile` | Icon container with per-icon hover/trigger motion (see `data-au-icon` names: at minimum `check, database, game, globe, mail, refresh, rocket, server, shield, spark` confirmed in the aurora-ui reference page; more exist across other pages, e.g. `bolt, backup, cpu, users` etc. seen in generator code). |
| Animated logo | `.au-logo` | Nxeon logo mark with a draw-on stroke animation (`.play`) and an idle periodic sheen sweep. |
| Count-up | `data-au-count` (JS in `aurora.js`/`aurora.built.js`, invoked from `part3.html`) | Numeric count-up with thousands separators; respects reduced motion (renders final value instantly). |

`aurora.js` (123 lines, unminified) vs `pages/aurora.built.js` (referenced by the build scripts as
the version actually inlined into dist pages) — the built version is what ships; I did not diff
them line-by-line but both exist side by side in `source/pages/`.

### Glass card tiers (documented in HANDOFF §3 and the design-system skill, pattern used throughout homepage/product pages, not a single CSS class)
- **Quiet** — neutral glass, product color only as a top hairline, lights up on hover (default for most cards).
- **Medium** — soft tint of the card's product color.
- **Vivid** — full glow, reserved for 1–2 focal cards per page (e.g. the homepage's featured VPS price card, the Creator panel).

## 5. Hardcoded / placeholder data

Scope: this document inventories **only** the new redesign package at
`/root/nxeon-marketing-v1/src/New Marketing Website v1/nxeon-website-handoff/`
(31 dist pages, the Python build system, assets, docs, skills). It does not audit the current
live nxeon.cloud site, the customer portal, or backend wiring — those are separate audits.

Everything below was verified by reading the actual files in this package
(`docs/HANDOFF.md`, `docs/OPEN-ITEMS.md`, `docs/url-map.json`, all four `skills/*/SKILL.md`,
every `dist/*.html`, every `source/pages/*/meta.json`, and the Python generators). Where I
inferred something rather than reading it directly, I've said so.

### Tokens (from `source/part1.html` `:root`, confirmed against `aurora.css`)

**Color:**
- Backgrounds: `--bg:#060913`, `--bg-2:#080D1C`, `--surface:#0C1328`, `--surface-2:#111A34`, `--surface-3:#16213F`
- Hairlines: `--line:rgba(138,160,255,.12)`, `--line-2:rgba(138,160,255,.2)`, `--line-3:rgba(160,180,255,.34)`
- Ink: `--ink:#E9EDFA`, `--ink-2:#B6BEDA`, `--muted:#8792B4`
- Brand/product: `--blue:#1463FF`, `--blue-hi:#3B7DFF`, `--link:#86A8FF`, `--indigo:#4B2EF2`
- Aurora accents: `--cyan:#3EDCF2`, `--purple:#7B3AF5`, `--magenta:#E04BD6`, `--green:#3FD89A`, `--amber:#F2B64B`
  (design-system skill docs also cite `#4E6BFF` blue, `#9B6BFF` violet, `#FF5FD7` magenta, `#FFD27A` amber as secondary shade variants used across pages — both are correct, these are 2-stop gradients per accent)
- Gradient: `--aurora: linear-gradient(90deg,#3EDCF2 0%,#0A66FF 36%,#4B2EF2 68%,#8B3DF5 100%)`
- `color-scheme: dark` is forced everywhere — **there is no light theme**; `:root[data-theme="light"]` is referenced defensively in a media query but no light-theme rule set exists in the files I found.

**Radii:** `--r-xl:24px; --r-lg:18px; --r-md:12px; --r-sm:8px` (plus Aurora's own `--au-r3` used on cards/buttons, defined in `aurora.css`).

**Type:** `--f-display` / `--f-body`: "Plus Jakarta Sans", system-ui fallback stack. `--f-mono`: "JetBrains Mono", ui-monospace fallback. Display weight 700–800, tight tracking ~ -0.04em per the skill doc (I did not measure this in CSS directly but it matches what's in `part1.html` heading rules).

**Layout:** `--container:1240px`, `--nav-h:68px`. Base font-size 17px, line-height 1.6.

Read directly from `aurora.css` selectors (249 lines) and cross-checked against the design-system
skill's own list. Every component below has a working CSS implementation in this file:

| Component | Selector(s) | One-line description |
|---|---|---|

| Button | `.au-btn` (+ `--glass`, `--ghost`) | Gradient pill button with an animated sheen sweep on hover; `--glass` variant adds a spinning conic-gradient border on hover; `--ghost` is bordered/transparent. Has `.is-loading` (spinner) and `.is-done` (green) states. |

| Text field | `.au-field` | Floating-label input/textarea with focus glow, inline hint text, a green "valid" check dot, and a shake animation on error. |
| Search box | `.au-search` | Pill search input with a `kbd` hint, clear button, and a blurred glow ring that grows in on focus. |
| Segmented control | `.au-seg` | Pill-group of buttons with a sliding "pill" background that animates between selections. |

| Chip / badge | `.au-chip` | Pill label with a pulsing status dot (`.d`); `.warn` variant recolors the dot amber. |
| Toast | `.au-toasts` / `.au-toast` | Bottom-right stacked toast notifications with an auto-dismiss progress bar; `auToast()` JS helper referenced in HANDOFF. |
| Progress bar | `.au-prog` | Bar with a shimmering highlight sweep animation. |
| Skeleton loader | `.au-skel` | Shimmering placeholder block for loading states. |
| Gauge | `.au-gauge` | Circular SVG gauge with lit tick marks and an animated count-up value in the center. |
| Sparkline | `.au-spark` | Small inline line chart with a hover point + tooltip. |
| Bar chart | `.au-bars` | Vertical animated bar chart, bars grow in on view, hoverable with value callouts. |
| Wave | `.au-wave` | Decorative animated SVG line/wave path. |
| Animated icon set | `.au-ic`, `data-au-icon`, `.au-tile` | Icon container with per-icon hover/trigger motion (see `data-au-icon` names: at minimum `check, database, game, globe, mail, refresh, rocket, server, shield, spark` confirmed in the aurora-ui reference page; more exist across other pages, e.g. `bolt, backup, cpu, users` etc. seen in generator code). |

`aurora.js` (123 lines, unminified) vs `pages/aurora.built.js` (referenced by the build scripts as
the version actually inlined into dist pages) — the built version is what ships; I did not diff
them line-by-line but both exist side by side in `source/pages/`.

### Glass card tiers (documented in HANDOFF §3 and the design-system skill, pattern used throughout homepage/product pages, not a single CSS class)
- **Quiet** — neutral glass, product color only as a top hairline, lights up on hover (default for most cards).
- **Medium** — soft tint of the card's product color.
- **Vivid** — full glow, reserved for 1–2 focal cards per page (e.g. the homepage's featured VPS price card, the Creator panel).

## 5. Hardcoded / placeholder data

### Confirmed by `docs/OPEN-ITEMS.md` as unconfirmed placeholders (section A) — reproduced here for completeness:
1. **Game-server tier prices**: Minecraft 1 GB $2.99 → 16 GB $32.99 (`TIERS` in `build_gameserver.py`, `GPRICE` in `pages/pricing/page.js`) — preview figures. Only Valheim's prices are marked live.
2. **Game-server vCPU/NVMe specs**: `SPEC = {1:(1,15), 2:(1,25), 4:(2,50), 6:(2,65), 8:(3,80), 12:(4,100), 16:(4,120)}` in `build_gs2.py` — modeled on VPS plans, not real, comment literally says "confirm with real specs".
3. **Fit-calculator / modpack sizing**: `PACK = {vanilla:[.5,.2,...], light:[.9,.22,...], modpack:[2,.26,...], heavy:[3.5,.32,...]}` in `pages/_gs3.js`, and `TINFO` in `build_gs2.py` — sizing heuristics, not measured.
4. **Review badges**: Trustpilot 4.9 (312 reviews), HostAdvice 4.8 (148), Google 4.9 (205) — confirmed present verbatim in `nxeon.html`, `nxeon-pricing.html`, `nxeon-minecraft-server-hosting.html`, `nxeon-minecraft-server-hosting-singapore.html` (`trust()` helper in `build_gs2.py` + hardcoded in homepage/pricing markup). Copied from the live site where they link to `#` — not yet linked to real profiles.
5. **Nav routes with no confirmed destination**: Dedicated IPv4 → `/vps#ipv4`; "AI apps and agents" → `/features` (same page as "Claude AI Builder" and "All features" — three different nav labels pointing at one placeholder route).
6. **Custom/enterprise route**: all custom-server CTAs go to `/contact?topic=custom`.
7. Routes marked **TBD** in `url-map.json`: NxCloud, both Minecraft × location pages, mods-browse page.
8. **Logged-in nav state** ("My account"/"Back to portal") is designed but not implemented — the nav always shows "Log in"/"Get started".

### Additional hardcoded data I found while reading the generators/dist directly (not called out in OPEN-ITEMS, worth the owner's attention):

- **VPS plan data** (`pages/pricing/page.js` `VPS` const): Starter 1vCPU/2GB/25GB $12.78, Standard 2vCPU/4GB/50GB $18.70, Pro 3vCPU/8GB/80GB $30.22, Max 4vCPU/16GB/120GB $47.50 — matches the "verified" figures the content-integrity skill lists, so these read as real, not placeholder, but they are still hardcoded JS constants that will drift from any live pricing change.
- **Web hosting plans** (`WEB` const): Starter $2.99, Business $4.99, Pro $8.99 (storage/sites/db/bandwidth figures also hardcoded).
- **Business email plans** (`MAIL` const): Starter $1.99 (1 box/5GB), Business $7.99 (5/10), Pro $24.99 (25/25).
- **Term discounts**: `TERM = {0:0, 12:0.2, 24:0.3, 36:0.4}` — 20/30/40% off for 1/2/3-year terms, hardcoded.
- **Non-Minecraft game sizing table** (`SZ` const in pricing `page.js`): min-GB/per-player/max-players heuristics hardcoded per game (rust, palworld, counterstrike2, projectzomboid, ark ×2, terraria, 7dtd, dayz, conanexiles, vrising, garrysmod, enshrouded, sonsoftheforest, satisfactory, factorio) — these are **not** flagged in OPEN-ITEMS but are exactly the same kind of heuristic as the flagged Minecraft SPEC table, and should probably be confirmed too.
- **NxLabs catalogue counts**: "64,709 mods across 33 games" (nxlabs hub), "32,252 verified Minecraft mods and plugins" (mods-minecraft / browse pages) — `games.json` (33 entries) and `mods.json` (42 sample entries) back the *shape* of this but the counts themselves are point-in-time numbers baked into copy; content-integrity skill explicitly says "Numbers are snapshots... production should read them from the live data."
- **Blog guide count mismatch**: `nxeon-blog.html` copy says "Over 330 guides from the team that runs the servers" and "search all 330+ guides", but the actual baked data (`build_bloghub.py`'s `P` list) only contains **25** posts, matching HANDOFF's own count ("the hub currently holds 25 real guides"). This is an internal inconsistency in the dist package itself, not just a live-site issue — worth flagging distinctly from the OPEN-ITEMS "issues found on the live site" list, since it's present in the *new* pages too.
- **DigitalOcean comparison pricing**: explicitly dated ("checked September 2026") inside `build_compare.py`'s `src` field — correctly caveated, but will need a refresh process before this page is trusted long-term.

- **Support SLA text**: contact page / meta.json say "reply within one business day" consistently in this new package — the content-integrity skill flags this as contradicting other parts of the *live* site's "24/7"/"around the clock" language; the dist pages themselves are internally consistent, but this needs a single source of truth decided before launch (this is an owner decision, not a build bug).

## 6. What's not done

**Pages/templates still to build (section B):**

Worth double-checking the ported homepage's own "global network"/`#network` visualization doesn't reintroduce extra cities.

This live-site naming inconsistency **is still present in the new pages** and should be fixed to "Claude Code" per the content-integrity skill's own instruction.

- **No 404 page, no legal pages (Terms/Privacy/AUP/SLA), no About/Status/Security/Developers/Docs page** exist anywhere in `dist/` or as a `source/pages/` folder — consistent with OPEN-ITEMS section B calling these out as "new designs" not yet started, but worth stating plainly: **zero legal pages exist today**, which is a launch blocker independent of design polish.

This should be flagged distinctly from "TBD" routes, since it's easy to miss in a visual QA pass (the link doesn't look broken, it just silently jumps to the wrong section).
- **Nav links to real-sounding but unbuilt nxeon.cloud routes**: `/block-storage`, `/vibe-coding`, `/tools`, `/developers`, `/features`, `/about`, `/security`, `/affiliate` are all linked directly (not via the `url-map.json` preview-link mechanism), meaning these are being treated as "already exist on production" — confirm that's actually true on the live site before porting, since several (Vibe coding, Features/Claude AI Builder, Free tools, Developers/API, Block Storage) are listed as **new, undesigned pages** in OPEN-ITEMS section B. If they don't exist live either, the nav will 404 on launch.
- **Dead source files**: `source/orbit2.js`, `source/home_glass.css`, `source/home_glass2.css` are present but unreferenced by any build script (see §3) — likely safe to ignore during porting, but worth a sanity check with the original builder in case they hold an intended future iteration.
- **`assets/tour/t1-4.webp`** — I could not trace these to a specific page/section in the time available; flagging as unaccounted-for rather than guessing.

### Accessibility / mobile — spot checks only (I did not run the Playwright verify/compare scripts from `nxeon-page-workflow`, since this is a read-only research task and those scripts render pages in a browser):
- `visually-hidden` utility class, skip-link (`.skip`), `aria-*` attributes on nav/menus/accordions/dialogs, and `prefers-reduced-motion` gating all appear consistently in the markup I read — the underlying markup looks accessibility-conscious.
- I did not verify actual rendered contrast, mobile layout overflow, or keyboard-trap behavior — the `nxeon-page-workflow` skill's own `scripts/verify_page.py` and `compare_screens.py` are the right tools for that and should be run before treating any page as launch-ready.
